briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin the Daily Climate Change Briefing for November 26, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Historic Breach of the '2°C Threshold' for Six Consecutive Days and the Deepening Climate Health Crisis
sections.content: In an unprecedented development, the global daily average temperature has surpassed the 2°C threshold above pre-industrial levels for six consecutive days for the first time in history [7, 87]. Notably, Monday recorded an increase of 2.24°C above the baseline, pushing global heating toward catastrophic levels [83, 87]. As heat-related fatalities hit record highs worldwide, international calls are mounting to declare climate change a global health emergency [6].

sections.title: ⚠️ Collapse of COP31 Negotiations and Discord in Global Climate Governance
sections.content: Global climate negotiations have dramatically collapsed after a coalition of nations rejected the proposed 'Antalya Agreement' at the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) [89]. OPEC blamed the European Union (EU) for the breakdown in talks, sparking a war of words, while the failure to reach an agreement on phasing out fossil fuels has fueled concerns over a retreat from the Paris Agreement and skepticism regarding coal phase-out efforts [12, 79]. In response, Pope Leo XIV expressed deep concern over the failure of COP31, defining climate change as a grave 'crisis' and calling for decisive action [66, 81].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 A Subtropical Shift in Agricultural Maps and the Dichotomy of Local Climate Adaptation
sections.content: On Jeju Island, cultivation has expanded beyond mangoes and bananas to include snack pineapples, rapidly redrawing the agricultural production map of the Korean Peninsula due to climate change [1]. Concurrently, responding to cold damage caused by erratic weather has become a decisive factor in annual harvest outcomes, elevating the importance of adaptation technologies [4]. However, even as field-oriented initiatives like Gyeonggi Province's 'Climate-Smart Agricultural Policy' gain traction, critics point to a disconnect between policy execution and financial support, highlighted by an 80% slash in the relevant budget [11, 13].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Evolves Through Community Benefit-Sharing and Technological Convergence
sections.content: In South Korea's energy transition landscape, community benefit-sharing power generation models are delivering tangible results [51, 59]. In Gimhae, South Gyeongsang Province, the nation's first 'Sunlight Income Village'—expected to generate 200 million won in annual revenue—has been completed and commenced commercial operation, while Pyeongchang County is also accelerating projects to return profits from a 150 MW solar power facility to local residents, following its wind power initiative [51, 55, 59]. In addition, institutional and technological advancements are progressing actively, including plans for a Jeju data center utilizing surplus renewable energy for AI computing workloads and briefing sessions on long-term contract bidding for new installations [46, 56].

briefing.closing: Even amid rising global temperatures and stalled multilateral negotiations, community-driven energy transitions and adaptation efforts continue steadily. That concludes today’s climate briefing.
